problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-4 & 6 & 1 & 1 \\ -6 & -5 & 4 & 0 \\ -5 & 3 & 3 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & 2 & 9\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}-4 & 6 & 1 & 1 \\ 10 & -29 & 0 & -4 \\ 7 & -15 & 0 & -2 \\ 9 & -11 & 0 & 7\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices $A$ and $B$ above. By applying three matrix elementary row operations 

- ${R}_{2}:={R}_{2}-4{R}_{1}$
- ${R}_{3}:=…$
- ${R}_{4}:=…$

each of the form ${R}_{i}:={R}_{i}+k{R}_{1},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the missing elementary row operations?

feedback.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 3 & -4 & 5 \\ 5 & -1 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 7 & 2 \\ 0 & 5 & 4 & -3\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}13 & 0 & 5 & 5 \\ 5 & -1 & 3 & 0 \\ 20 & 0 & 19 & 2 \\ 25 & 0 & 19 & -3\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices $A$ and $B$ above. By applying three matrix elementary row operations 

- ${R}_{1}:=…$
- ${R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+4{R}_{2}$
- ${R}_{4}:=…$

each of the form ${R}_{i}:={R}_{i}+k{R}_{2},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the missing elementary row operations?
feedback.worked_solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make entries above and below ${a}_{22}=-1$ equal to $0.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary row operations:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & 3 & -4 & 5 \\ 5 & -1 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 7 & 2 \\ 0 & 5 & 4 & -3\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+3{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}13 & 0 & 5 & 5 \\ 5 & -1 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 7 & 2 \\ 0 & 5 & 4 & -3\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+4{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}13 & 0 & 5 & 5 \\ 5 & -1 & 3 & 0 \\ 20 & 0 & 19 & 2 \\ 0 & 5 & 4 & -3\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{4}:={R}_{4}+5{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}13 & 0 & 5 & 5 \\ 5 & -1 & 3 & 0 \\ 20 & 0 & 19 & 2 \\ 25 & 0 & 19 & -3\end{aligned}] \\  & =B\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the missing elementary row operations are

$\,$ ${R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+3{R}_{2}\,$ and $\,{R}_{4}:={R}_{4}+5{R}_{2}.$
